correctness.rationale: The finite sine sum gives (H_du)_i=cos((i-1/2)theta_k)/(2 sin(theta_k/2)); the proposed sine vector equals (-1)^(k-1) times that cosine vector. Its eigenvalues are ordered by decreasing magnitude, not algebraic size, and have alternating signs. Alternatively H=U J for unit upper triangular summation matrix U and reversal J, so H^(-1)=J(I-S) for upper shift S. Its square is the tridiagonal first-difference Gram matrix with cos((i-1/2)theta_k) modes. Full column rank permits rectangular congruence after extending a basis, giving exactly n-d additional zeros. For every B, loading is equivalent to H+eta I being PSD (take B=I); k=2 is the most negative eigenvalue, including d=2. In a symmetric binary PSD supermask, all entries in row one are one, forcing all diagonal entries to be one by principal minors. The zero quadratic forms on e_1-e_j then force every column to equal the first. The d(d-1)/2 additions count ordered products. The geometric positive-vector example has invertible B for q>0 and each missing product has norm at most (d+3)q^d; the full Gram norm is at least d+3. For fixed d the relative error goes to zero while negative inertia persists. The d=2 determinant is -9q^2. Independent bounded check: 63 inverse spectra (d=2 through 64) and exact negative principal-minor witnesses for all strict completions among 598 binary masks (d=2 through 6), via python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_records_1_to_4.py. The universal claims follow from proof, not these ranges. Frozen verification and same-model evidence were read, not counted as independent experiments.

evidence: The squared kernel has simple eigenvalues. Once its cosine modes are known, H acts scalarly on each one; comparing the last coordinate of H u (which is u_1) with u_d fixes the sign directly. The smallest signed eigenvalue then immediately gives the sharp scalar loading. The finite-precision schedule citation does not assert arbitrary split-vector attainability.

The scientifically distinct part is the complete diagnosis of what can be done without scalar loading and the construction of an arbitrarily small-error but cone-violating family in the stated surrogate. The rigidity argument uses an elementary general PSD property, and is not claimed as new PSD matrix theory.

value.rationale: For a motivated truncation schedule the result distinguishes normwise approximation from cone preservation in a complete ideal Gram model. It answers two distinct design questions with sharp boundaries: a scalar coefficient shift works at a precise cutoff, whereas a binary completion cannot save any omitted products. The positive, full-rank small-error example establishes that the obstruction is not limited to large relative error or mixed-sign inputs. No hardware or optimal accuracy claim is required or supported.
